Header: Fimbristylis miliaceae syn. of F. quinquangularis (accepted name) and Fimbristylis littoralis (accepted name) Myet-kun-thee-lay

Prevention: Clean tools and farm machinery when leaving an infested area to prevent seeds being spread; especially important if the weed is not yet in the area
Seeds are spread by livestock do not allow them to transfer seeds to uninfested areas
Prepare land by deep ploughing (>12cm) to bury and/or dessicate the weed seed before planting
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: pulses, Sesame, groundnut, sunflower, maize
Tufted leafy annual or perennial erect sedge with fibrous root system (up to 80-90cm high).
Leaves dark green and stiff; inflorescence a rather lax and diffuse compound umbel, 6-10 cm long; shoots of young plants flattened (laterally compressed) at base
Check fields two weeks after sowing for the level of weed infestation
Consider direct control if weed is present
Direct Control: Hand weeding and mechanical hoeing can give good control, especially under dry conditions
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
